ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $E$ is on the side $CD$ of rectangle $ABCD$. The rectangle $ABCD$ is folded along $AE$ so that point $D$ falls on point $F$ on side $BC$. If $AB=6$ and $AD=10$, what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore AD=BC=10$, $AB=CD=6$,\\
Folding rectangle $ABCD$ along line $AE$, vertex $D$ precisely falls on point $F$ on side $BC$,\\
$\therefore AF=AD=10$, $EF=DE$,\\
In $\triangle ABF$, $BF=\sqrt{AF^{2}-AB^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}=8$,\\
$\therefore CF=BC-BF=10-8=2$,\\
Let $CE=x$, then $DE=EF=6-x$,\\
In $\triangle ECF$, $CE^{2}+FC^{2}=EF^{2}$,\\
$\therefore x^{2}+2^{2}=(6-x)^{2}$,\\
Solving for $x$ gives $x=\frac{8}{3}$,\\
$\therefore DE=6-x=\boxed{\frac{10}{3}}$.
